subjects.name: This and That
subjects.summary: Esse/essa/isso for this, aquele/aquela/aquilo for that, plus the plurals esses/essas and aqueles/aquelas. Isso and aquilo refer to unknown things or things that are not physical.

subjects.name: Contractions with De
subjects.summary: De contracts with demonstratives: disso, desse, dessa, daquilo, daquele, daquela. Required after verbs and expressions that take de, such as gostar de, precisar de, and medo de.

subjects.name: Simple Past
subjects.summary: Regular past endings for -ar, -er, and -ir verbs, plus irregular preterite forms of ir, trazer, ver, fazer, ter, dizer, and pedir.

subjects.name: Was and Were
subjects.summary: Estava for past location, feelings, and ongoing actions. Era for lasting past states. Foi for a single completed situation.

subjects.name: Past Habits
subjects.summary: Perfeito for one completed action. Imperfeito, or costumar, for habits and repeated past actions.

subjects.name: Past Participles
subjects.summary: Passive voice with ser + participle, compared with the active preterite. Includes regular and irregular participles.

subjects.name: Because of This
subjects.summary: Por isso for that's why, por causa disso/daquilo for because of this/that, and devido a/ao for due to.

subjects.name: Ordinal Numbers
subjects.summary: Ordinals from primeiro through centésimo, used for floors, rankings, and the nth time.

subjects.name: Para and Por
subjects.summary: Para for goal, destination, opinion, and deadline. Por for agent, rate, duration, reason, and movement through. Contractions pelo, pela, pelos, pelas.

subjects.name: Nouns Ending in -ão
subjects.summary: Nouns that end in -ão, and how their plurals tend to work.

grammar.title: Isso, esse, essa / aquilo, aquele, aquela
grammar.explanation: Esse and essa point to something near the idea of 'this' and agree in gender. Aquilo and aquele/aquela point to 'that'. Use isso and aquilo when you do not know what the thing is, or when it is not a physical object, such as a situation or a piece of information. The teacher also lists isto, este, and esta as words that can be used the same way.

examples.portuguese: Essa menina é minha irmã.
examples.english: This girl is my sister.

examples.portuguese: Eu não sei o que é isso.
examples.english: I don't know what this is.

examples.portuguese: Aquele homem é meu pai.
examples.english: That man is my father.

examples.portuguese: Aquilo não é verdade.
examples.english: That is not true.

grammar.usageNote: Everyday speech uses isso, esse, and essa.

grammar.title: Contractions with de
grammar.explanation: De combines with the demonstratives. Verbs and expressions that need de make the contraction mandatory. The teacher contrasts the split form, which should not be said, with the contracted form.

examples.portuguese: Eu não gosto disso.
examples.english: I don't like this.

examples.portuguese: Eu gosto muito desse livro.
examples.english: I really like this book.

examples.portuguese: Eu sou dessa cidade.
examples.english: I'm from this city.

examples.portuguese: Não gostei daquilo que vi.
examples.english: I didn't like what I saw.

exceptions.wrong: Eu gosto muito de esse livro.

grammar.title: Verbs and expressions that take de
grammar.explanation: These verbs keep the preposition de, which then contracts with the following article or demonstrative.
patterns: cuidar de = to take care of
aproximar de = to get closer to
medo de = to be afraid of

examples.portuguese: Eu estou com medo desse cachorro.
examples.english: I'm afraid of this dog.

examples.portuguese: Não esqueça disso amanhã.
examples.english: Don't forget about this tomorrow.

grammar.title: Adjective gender and emphasis
grammar.explanation: Adjectives agree with the noun. Many masculine forms end in -o and the feminine ends in -a. Muito means very or a lot. Um pouco means a little.

examples.portuguese: Meu chefe é estressado.
examples.english: My boss is stressed.

examples.portuguese: Essa casa é feia e suja.
examples.english: This house is ugly and dirty.

examples.portuguese: Hoje está um pouco frio.
examples.english: Today is a bit cold.

grammar.title: Comparatives and superlatives
grammar.explanation: Mais or menos plus the adjective plus que or do que means more or less than. The superlative uses o, a, os, or as plus mais. Grande, pequeno, bom, and mau/ruim do not take mais.

examples.portuguese: O Brasil é maior do que a França.
examples.english: Brazil is bigger than France.

examples.portuguese: Ela é mais alta do que eu.
examples.english: She is taller than me.

examples.portuguese: São Paulo é a maior cidade do Brasil.
examples.english: São Paulo is the biggest city in Brazil.

examples.portuguese: Caipirinha é a melhor bebida do bar.
examples.english: Caipirinha is the best drink at the bar.

grammar.title: Color agreement
grammar.explanation: Some colors agree in gender. Preto, branco, vermelho, amarelo, and roxo take -a in the feminine. Colors that are also nouns, such as rosa, laranja, and azul, stay invariable in these lessons.

examples.portuguese: Minha cama é preta.
examples.english: My bed is black.

examples.portuguese: O céu é azul.
examples.english: The sky is blue.

grammar.title: Então, tão, and tanto
grammar.explanation: Então connects a sequence or a result: then or so. Desde então means since then. Tão intensifies an adjective: so. Tanto agrees: tanto, tanta, tantos, tantas. Tanto faz means it doesn't matter. Tanto quanto means as much as.

examples.portuguese: Eu vou para a academia e então eu vou trabalhar.
examples.english: I go to the gym and then I go to work.

grammar.title: Tempo, vez, época, hora, horário, clima
grammar.explanation: Tempo asks how long and also means weather. Vez is an occasion or a turn. Às vezes and de vez em quando mean sometimes. De vez means for good. Época is a period or season. Hora is clock time. Horário is a schedule or appointment. Clima is weather, mood, or vibe.

examples.english: How long will you stay here?

examples.english: The party atmosphere was really lively.

grammar.title: Regular simple past
grammar.explanation: Regular verbs are grouped by the infinitive ending. In the preterite, -ar verbs use -ei, -ou, -amos, -aram. -er verbs use -i, -eu, -emos, -eram. -ir verbs use -i, -iu, -imos, -iram. The lesson also shows the present and the present continuous (estar + gerund) next to the past.

examples.portuguese: Eu falei com ela ontem.
examples.english: I spoke to her yesterday.

examples.portuguese: Eu comi comida japonesa ontem.
examples.english: I ate Japanese food yesterday.

examples.portuguese: Eu saí de casa ontem.
examples.english: I left home yesterday.

grammar.title: Foi, era, and estava
grammar.explanation: Estar in the imperfect (estava) is for location, emotions, and actions in progress. Ser in the imperfect (era) is for what something was like over a long period. Ser in the preterite (foi) is for a single event or situation that is over.

examples.portuguese: Eu estava na academia.
examples.english: I was at the gym.

examples.portuguese: Quando eu era criança, eu era muito tímido.
examples.english: When I was a child, I was very shy.

examples.portuguese: A festa foi boa.
examples.english: The party was good.

examples.portuguese: Ontem foi um dia muito especial.
examples.english: Yesterday was a very special day.

grammar.title: Perfeito versus imperfeito
grammar.explanation: The preterite states one finished action. The imperfect states a habit or something that continued in the past. Costumar plus the infinitive is another way to say used to.
patterns: eu costumava + infinitive = I used to

examples.portuguese: Eu conversei com ela ontem.
examples.english: I talked to her yesterday.

examples.portuguese: Eu conversava muito com ela na universidade.
examples.english: I used to talk to her a lot at university.

examples.portuguese: Eu costumava viajar sozinho.
examples.english: I used to travel by myself.

grammar.title: Participle and passive voice
grammar.explanation: Ser plus the participle makes a passive sentence. The participle agrees with the subject. Regular -ar participles end in -ado/-ada, and regular -er/-ir participles end in -ido/-ida. Several common verbs are irregular, including aberto, escrito, feito, dito, and visto.

examples.portuguese: O carro foi comprado pelo vizinho.
examples.english: The car was bought by the neighbor.

examples.portuguese: O vizinho comprou o carro.
examples.english: The neighbor bought the car.

examples.portuguese: A música foi cantada no show.
examples.english: The song was sung at the concert.

grammar.title: Por isso, por causa, devido a
grammar.explanation: Por isso means that's why. Por causa disso, desse, dessa, daquilo, daquele, or daquela means because of this or that. Devido a, and the contraction devido ao, means due to.
patterns: devido a / devido ao = due to

examples.portuguese: Ele está cansado e por isso não quer ir na festa.
examples.english: He's tired and that's why he doesn't want to go to the party.

examples.portuguese: Por causa da chuva, eu não vou viajar.
examples.english: Because of the rain, I won't travel.

examples.portuguese: Devido à chuva, eu não vou viajar.
examples.english: Due to the rain, I won't travel.

grammar.title: Ordinal numbers
grammar.explanation: Ordinals agree in gender: primeiro/primeira, décimo/décima. They are used for position, the floor of a building, and the nth time something happens. Último means the last one.

examples.portuguese: Meu apartamento fica no sétimo andar.
examples.english: My apartment is on the seventh floor.

examples.portuguese: Essa é a vigésima vez que vou ao Brasil.
examples.english: This is the twentieth time I've been to Brazil.

grammar.title: Para and por
grammar.explanation: Para covers a goal, a destination, an opinion, and a deadline. Por covers the agent of a passive, a rate, a length of time, a reason, and movement through or around. Por contracts with articles: pelo, pela, pelos, pelas. Spoken Brazilian Portuguese often uses pra and pro.
patterns: para mim = in my opinion / for me
por + period = for a length of time

grammar.title: Parts of the day, and late versus early
grammar.explanation: De manhã, de tarde, and de noite say when something happens. Ontem, hoje, and amanhã combine with those parts of the day. Está tarde means the hour is late. Estou atrasado means the person is late. Cedo means early.
patterns: de manhã / pela manhã = in the morning
de tarde / pela tarde = in the afternoon
de noite / pela noite = at night

examples.portuguese: Hoje eu não vou trabalhar de manhã.
examples.english: Today I won't work in the morning.

examples.portuguese: Eles foram na biblioteca ontem à noite.
examples.english: They went to the library last night.

examples.portuguese: Eu perdi o trem porque eu estava atrasado.
examples.english: I missed the train because I was late.

exceptions.note: A person is atrasado. The hour is tarde.

exceptions.wrong: Estou atrasado para say the clock is late.
